minutes_text:
CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 14, 2021 - 4:30 P .M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:47 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Councilmember Kennedy.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19 in Pasadena, the nation, and around the world.

PUBLIC COMMENT  Stephanie Miller, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City to
  amend its regulations related to construction hours to commence
  at 8:00 a.m. in residential neighborhoods.

  Mayor Gordo responded that staff will reach out to Ms. Miller to
  address her concerns.

  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
  to move forward with the rezoning of land owned by churches and
  other religious organizations to allow for building and providing
  affordable housing.

  The following individuals requested that the narrated video of the
  officer involved shooting of Anthony McClain be removed from the
  City's website; expressed concerns with the Pasadena Police
  Department and policing, spoke against the increased violence in
  the City; advocated for the termination of Pasadena Police Chief
  Perez, Officers Dumaguindin and Sereno, and City Manager Steve
  Mermell; spoke on controversial incidents involving Pasadena
  police officers, expressed concerns with the time limitations related
  to public comment, and/or raised concerns regarding the selected
  Independent Police Auditor (IPA):

Council Minutes  06/14/2021
   Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Jason Reedy, Los Angeles resident
  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing Black Lives Matter
  Adriana Bautista, Pasadena resident
  Michael Williams, Pasadena resident
  Kerwin Manning, Pasadena resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, provided information on the community
  opportunities to provide "Public Comment" during the City Council
  meetings, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated to allow all individuals who
  submitted a public speaker card to speak during "Public Comment
  On Matters Not On The Agenda," but suggested that the time be
  decreased so that all speakers are allowed to speak at the
  beginning of the City Council meeting.

  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO ANNUAL SOFTWARE
  MAINTENANCE  ANO  SUPPORT  CONTRACTS  WITH
  INTELLITIME SYSTEMS CORPORATIONS FOR THE CITY'S
  VIRTUAL TIMECARO INTERFACE (VTI) SYSTEM
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed contract is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3);
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract without
  competitive bidding pursuant to City Charter Section 1002(F),
  contracts for professional or unique services, with lntellitime
  Systems Corporation for software maintenance and support for the
  City's Virtual Timecard Interface (VTI) system in an amount not-to-
  exceed $91,250 for the twelve month period beginning July 1,2021;
  (3) Grant the proposed contract an exemption from the
  Competitive Selection process pursuant to Pasadena Municipal
  Code Section 4.08.049(8) contracts for which the City's best
  interests are served; and
  (4) Authorize the City Manager to execute future annual
  maintenance and support contracts, including an amount for any
  as-needed services, for as long as the City utilizes the VTI system.
  (Note to Legislative File: this item was processed as a Purchase

PUBLIC HEARING  PUBLIC HEARING: ZONING CODE AMENDMENT TO PARKING
  REQUIREMENTS FOR ADDITIONS TO SINGLE-FAMILY
  RESIDENCES
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the Zoning Code Amendments are exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to Section
  15305 (Class 5 - Minor Alterations to Land Use Limitations) and
  that there are no features that distinguish this project from others in
  the exempt class, there are no unusual circumstances, and none of
  the exceptions to the exemptions apply;
  (2) Adopt the Findings of Consistency with the General Plan
  (Attachment A of the agenda report); and

Council Minutes  11  06/14/2021
   (3) Approve the amendment and direct the City Attorney to
  prepare an ordinance amending Section 17.46.020 of Title 17
  (Zoning Code) of the Pasadena Municipal Code to exempt additions
  of any size to existing single-family residences from the two-car
. .,  covered parking requirement, except for residences located within
  an HD Overlay Zone (Attachment B of the agenda report).

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that
  the public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Press on
  May 31, June 3, 2021, and June 10, 2021, and in the Pasadena
  Journal on June 3, 2021, and June 10, 2021; and 1 email in support
  of the staff recommendation, which was distributed to the City
  Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public record.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  provided introductory comments, and Andre Sahakian, Senior
  Planner, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson suggested the proposed action allow additions
  to single-family dwellings of up to 500 square feet, or some other
  cap, to be exempt from the requirement of providing two covered
  parking spaces; and to allow for parking in a driveway and/or
  carport as an alternative. He also suggested that additions to single-
  family dwellings of 1,200 square feet or more should abide by the
  requirement of providing two covered parking spaces.

  Councilmember Hampton spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, and stated that he believes the required covered
  parking requirement is unreasonable. He spoke in favor of allowing
  property owners who have space on their property to determine
  where to park vehicles and that it not be tied to building additions or
  Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU's).

  Christine McLaughlin, Pasadena resident, spoke in favor of
  the staff recommendation.

  Councilmember Williams spoke on the need for the City Council to
  consider why the parking requirements were put in place, which she
  believes is to preserve the safety of City streets. She expressed
  concerns with homeowners who build additions and ADU's but are
  unable to acquire overnight parking permits. She spoke in favor of
  allowing additions to single-family dwellings of more than 500
  square feet to be required to provide parking onsite. In addition,
  Councilmember Williams stated that she does not believe the
  findings for the Zoning Code Text Amendment (referenced in
  Attachment A of the agenda report), can be made, specifically
  Finding No. 2: "The proposed amendment would not be detrimental
  to the public interest, health, safety convenience or general welfare

  Council Minutes  12  06/ 14/2021
   to the City" due to public safety concerns created by vehicle street
  parking on the more narrow streets of the City.

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's request, Mr. Reyes
  summarized the recommended changes suggested by Vice Mayor
  Wilson and Councilmember Williams, as follows: for additions or
  ADU construction of up to 500 square feet - no covered parking
  would be required; for construction of more than 500 square feet
  but less than 1,200 square feet - staff to conduct a parking study to
  determine if adequate parking existed at the property (i.e. drive way,
  tandem, side yard); and for construction of more than 1,200 square
  feet - two covered parking spaces would continue to be required ,
  which he believes adequately addresses the concerns of smaller
  single family residential dwellings not being able to reasonably build
  additions.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Wilson,
  seconded by Councilmember Williams, to close the public hearing:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  removal of the narrated video of the officer involved shooting of
  Anthony McClain from the City's website; and the legality of
  agendizing that matter and the termination of the officer involved in
  the shooting of Anthony McClain, as a personnel matter, City
  Attorney Bagneris responded that pursuant to the City Charter,
  directing the discipline of an employee who is under the purview of
  the City Manager is not permissible. She also responded that in
  terms of the narrated video of the officer involved shooting, the City
  Council can review the policy of what is posted on the City's
  website, and that it would take five votes of the City Council to direct
  the City Manager to change the policy. She also noted that such an
  issue can be addressed during the City Manager's evaluation.

  and asked the City Attorney to consider the City Council's options
  related to the removal of the narrated video from the City's website,
  and an informational presentation on the City's Charter and state
  law as to the City Council's authority to agendize for discussion and
